# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

THIRZA journeyed to town the following day and came back when it was evening. Nell had traveled across to Pear Hill alongside Isolde and returned to discover Thirza inside the kitchen, where she was seated beside the table, her head resting upon her hand. A feeling of dread pierced Nell's heart because of something about her dispirited posture. Never before had she observed Thirza sitting in such a weakly motionless manner.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0000 }

“Are you extremely weary, Thirza?”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0001 }

“Yes—no—I don’t know,” Thirza replied exhaustedly, glancing upward. “I guess I am fatigued, though I haven’t given it any thought. That isn’t the issue.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0002 }

“Have you been to the oculist? What were his words?” Nell inquired with concern.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0003 }

“Yes, I saw him. My eyes were examined by him. According to him, provided that I completely abandon reading and sewing along with every type of eye-straining labor, refrain from crying, and use the glasses he provided, he believes my eyes might refrain from deteriorating further and my headaches will be healed. However, should I fail to do so, he states that I will definitely become stone-blind within six months. Blind! Nell, just imagine that!”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0004 }

Nell remained quiet for a moment following her initial swift cry of distress. She felt as though speech was impossible for her. Subsequently, she spoke courageously, though a sob quavered in her breath:
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0005 }

“Thirza, do not contemplate that. You are aware that he has offered you hope. Should you exercise caution, your vision will not be entirely lost; moreover, if your headaches are remedied by his glasses, that will be an incredible outcome.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0006 }

“I do not consider that much hope,” Thirza stated with bitterness. “If I am unable to read, sew, or perform any similar tasks, what reason do I have to go on living? I may as well be without sight—or deceased. Regarding my weeping, I am unable to prevent it whenever solitude overtakes me. Nevertheless, discussing the matter serves no purpose. Should you fetch me a cup of tea, I would appreciate it. I am nearly exhausted. Avoid mentioning any of this to anyone for a time, at least. I am unable to endure people coming here to interrogate, offer sympathy, and converse regarding it.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0007 }

After Thirza finished her midday meal, Nell convinced her to retire to bed. Subsequently, Nell made her way to the east gable, where she took a seat near her window in the dark, accompanied only by her weeping and a heavy heart. What a melancholy transformation had taken place since she occupied that same spot the evening following her return home! At that earlier time, she was brimming with hope and happiness, and what lay ahead appeared bright with potential. Nell experienced a sensation of having aged many years in the interim, yet prior to falling asleep, a smile touched her lips and serenity filled her heart. She had bravely confronted her obligation and discovered it to be a companion—just as duty always proves to be whenever we encounter it with honesty.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0008 }

A couple of days afterward, during one afternoon, Thirza entered slowly from the front yard, having been speaking there to a visitor—a male whom Nell recognized by sight as Sadler of Delford. Nell pondered what the man might have told Thirza to cause such an expression to appear on her face.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0009 }

“What was Mr. Sadler looking for, Thirza?”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0010 }

Taking a seat beside the window, Thirza gazed upon Nell. Disregarding the injunction of the oculist, tears filled her eyes, and her tone faltered when she spoke:
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0011 }

“It came to his attention that Grey Shutters was to be sold by me, and he desires to purchase it.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0012 }

“Purchase it! Purchase Grey Shutters?” Nell questioned whether her ears had deceived her. “Oh, Thirza, you cannot intend to part with Grey Shutters!”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0013 }

“I am at a loss for any other solution, Nell, though I have pondered the entire situation. Had my eyesight remained good, remaining here to handle the management alongside a capable hired hand would have been possible. My current condition prevents that, however. My vision might vanish completely, and regardless, running this place is beyond my ability now. Ah, the thought that I would survive to witness the time I must part with my own home never crossed my mind. Yet matters will simply deteriorate continuously until the property becomes entirely unmarketable. That bank failure absorbed every bit of our funds, and certain notes that Obed signed previous autumn still require payment. Selling this place and securing lodging elsewhere—likely at her house—is the course Mrs. Sowerby recommends. Given its limited size and aged structures, the price it fetches will be low. Still, I calculate it should yield sufficient funds for my maintenance. It is a relief to me that the scholarship secures your needs, Nell. My sole regret is that no home will remain for your vacation visits, though I assume you will find a way to get by.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0014 }

Thirza lost control of her emotions and cried profusely.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0015 }

“It is imperative that you do not part with Grey Shutters,” Nell stated with firm determination.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0016 }

“Oh, Nell, I wish it weren't necessary for me to do so. But you are able to observe the situation on your own. Staying here by myself is impossible for me. Trouble and loneliness would drive me out of my mind. And my vision would be lost—of that I am certain.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0017 }

“Thirza, you will not be required to remain in this place by yourself. I will stay by your side. I have no intention of traveling to Wexcombe.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0018 }

“Not going to Wexcombe!” Raising her lined face out of her hands, Thirza gazed at Nell. “Why, what do you mean?”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0019 }

“It is exactly what I am saying. Taking the scholarship is not something I am going to do. The decision was made by me the evening following your return from town. Surely you cannot believe I would abandon you in your distress, Thirza, considering everything you have done on my behalf. My mind has been busy thinking and planning. Allow me to explain my intentions to you. A lease on the farm for the coming year is desired by Mr. Pembroke. Consequently, no trouble will be caused to you by that matter. Furthermore, teaching will be my occupation. An application has been submitted by me for the local school—though obtaining it is not expected by me because my understanding is that the trustees pledged the position to Hugh Carrow. However, the school in Delford is available to me—I was informed of this by Mr. Blair yesterday evening at the store. Naturally, having the Brierley school would be somewhat nicer and more convenient. Nevertheless, remaining at home for board and driving back and forth to Delford will be possible for me, at least during the warmer months. Even throughout the winter season, returning home on Fridays will be manageable for me. A horse will be retained by us for that purpose. Ah, every detail has been arranged by me, Thirza. Additionally, reading to you and maintaining your spirits will be done by me. Dullness or lonesomeness will not be suffered by you. Moreover, genuine coziness and happiness will be shared here between us, you and me.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0020 }

Thirza had paid attention in the manner of a female inside a dream.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0021 }

“Oh, Nell, I know I could manage quite fine with you present. However, I am unable to permit you to make such a sacrifice on my behalf. That would be awful.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0022 }

“Nonsense!” Nell chuckled joyously. “It isn't a sacrifice. Nothing is worse than losing Grey Shutters—no injury could be greater to me. We have to retain the beloved old home. Thirza, I have completely decided. Wexcombe is not where I am going; instead, I shall remain in this place to instruct. Do not fret over me at all.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0023 }

“Yet your desires—and—”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0024 }

“My ambition remains every bit as strong as before. However, the goal of my ambitions has shifted. My aim is to become a fine teacher—and to preserve your sight. In addition, I intend to learn here at home, completing a small college course entirely on my own. Oh, my plans are numerous, Thirza. I have spent a week working them out. My finest efforts will be devoted to life here, and I trust that it will offer its finest back to me. Upon leaving Regent’s, my future appeared to lie ahead of me like an unbending path. It seemed I could look down it past numerous milestones. At present, it contains a turn. What exists past the turn is unknown to me, yet I will hold to the belief that the finest things do. That turn possesses its very own appeal, Thirza. I speculate about the path’s course past it—the green magnificence and gentle, dappled lights and darks that exist there—the unfamiliar vistas—the unfamiliar splendors—the bends, rises, and hollows farther ahead.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0025 }

“I don’t feel as though I should allow you to surrender it,” said Thirza, speaking about the scholarship.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0026 }

“However, you are unable to stop me. My age is sixteen and a half, and I am ‘obstinate as a mule,’ just as Mrs. Sowerby informed me at one time,” Nell laughed. “Oh, Thirza, avoid pitying me. Being pitied is not to my liking, nor is there any occasion for it. The mere idea of remaining at beloved Grey Shutters makes my heart glad. It could not be loved by anyone the way you and I love it—consequently, we have to preserve it.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0027 }

“You blessed girl!” Thirza said, giving in. “I feel as if you’ve given new life to me. I guess I ought to hold out and force you to attend college—yet I know I am unable to, so I will not attempt it. I will make amends to you though, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0028 }

Once word spread throughout Brierley that Nell Harcourt was no longer planning on attending college, choosing instead to remain at home to teach, the matter sparked considerable debate. The majority of the kindly townspeople, who were unaware of Thirza’s eye trouble, considered her decision unwise. Mrs. Wace held a different view. She expressed her commendation to Nell using encouraging remarks that made the girl weep with joy. Kindly Mrs. Sowerby felt the same way. She paid a visit one night and discovered Nell together with Thirza resting by the front entrance during the balmy, fragrant summer twilight. They enjoyed resting in that spot as night fell, white moths flitted through the garden, and the scent of mint saturated the damp air.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0029 }

Releasing a drawn-out sigh that combined fatigue and comfort, Mrs. Agatha seated her heavy body on the bench made of stone beside the entrance, backed by a line of high hollyhocks in shades of pink and yellow.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0030 }

“I must say I am becoming pleased to take a seat. My feet have carried me the whole day, and two hundred pounds is quite a weight for just two feet to haul about. Not being overweight is a major blessing, Thirza. I trust you are grateful for it. Now, Nell, word has reached me that you abandoned your plan to attend college. Hearing that made me genuinely pleased. You currently possess as much learning as is good for a woman’s comfort. Girls attending college alongside men and filling their brains with Latin and Greek and such foolishness is something I do not support.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0031 }

“However, I shall still learn Greek and Latin, Mrs. Sowerby,” Nell stated with a laugh. “My intention is to complete my Arts degree right here at Grey Shutters, pursuing all the subjects that I would have taken at university.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0032 }

In sacred dismay, Mrs. Sowerby raised her hands.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0033 }

“Nell Harcourt, you’ll end up dead.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0034 }

“Far from it. It will do me good. Oh, I do not intend to push myself too hard. I will be ‘mejum,’ just as ‘Josiah Allen’s wife,’ remarks. However, the lengthy winter nights will give me plenty of free time, and I am not suited for fancy work. You know, I am taking up a teaching position over at Delford.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0035 }

“I’m not aware of it. My assumption is that your teaching will take place directly here in Brierley. You have been selected by the trustees to receive the school.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0036 }

“Mrs. Sowerby!” Nell exclaimed, leaping up because she was so astonished. “Why, it was my impression that Hugh Carrow had been promised it!”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0037 }

“Indeed they did. However, the moment Hugh learned you had put in for the position, he approached them—you see, they held a business gathering at the schoolhouse yesterday evening—and informed them he was revoking his own application, while recommending yours instead. He stated that Pale Sands would be his teaching location. Naturally, he recognized the depth of your desire to remain alongside Thirza, and I feel compelled to state that it struck me as truly generous and considerate on his part, indeed it was. Truly self-denying as well, because paying for board will be necessary for him at Pale Sands, and his need to fund his own path through college is common knowledge. Consequently, the trustees resolved to select you. I experienced sheer delight when Thomas arrived home and informed me.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0038 }

“I feel I shouldn’t accept it,” Nell whispered. “What I mean is—I doubt I should allow Hugh to make a sacrifice like that for—for my sake.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0039 }

“I suppose it is impossible to stop him at this point. Papers have been signed by him with the trustees from Pale Sands. Therefore, your refusal at this juncture would not benefit him in the least. Naturally, the school will be taken by you. Things will go smoothly enough for you, seeing that no Tulks are attending any longer. The final one among them was Flossie, and it is certainly a blessing, that is my opinion. A succession of Tulks has attended Brierley school over the past twenty years, and I suspect they existed solely to ensure school teachers remembered that earth is not where they belong. Goodness gracious! What is the purpose of all that blinking and winking over at the Pembroke gable?”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0040 }

“Isolde is using signals to ask me to visit,” Nell said with a laugh. “You are aware that we maintain that traditional habit. Please pardon me as I hurry across to find out what her request is.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0041 }

Leaping down the grassy incline as swiftly as a deer, Nell vanished into the piney darkness of the Whispering Wood. Mrs. Sowerby watched her depart with an affectionate gaze.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0042 }

“In certain respects, she still has a lot of the youngster in her.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0043 }

“She exhibits a great deal more of her womanhood when she is around other people,” Thirza snapped back, briefly regaining her previous sharpness.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0044 }

Yet Thirza was no longer characterized by crispness. This was what Mrs. Sowerby remarked to her Thomas on that evening.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0045 }

“Thirza Abernethy has turned mellow. That is the reason.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0046 }

Nell traveled to the small Brierley graveyard the following evening so that she could place new blossoms upon Obed’s grave and give water to the Scotch rosebush. She tarried in that spot until evening fell, finding pleasure in the tranquility and quiet of the small site, featuring poplars that rustled like quiet, welcoming conversation, alongside murmuring grasses expanding freely between the graves. By the time she eventually departed and journeyed down the extensive hill descending toward the Lake of Glassy Waters, the sun had set and the entirety of Brierley stretched out in front of her inside an ethereal twilight—“a haunt of ancient peace.” A crispness filled the atmosphere resembling a breeze that had swept across honey-sweet clover fields. Residences' lights began to gleam here and there through the farmstead trees. Farther off stretched the ocean, hazy and violet, emitting its evocative, perpetual rumble. The western sky formed a splendor of gentle blended tones, while the pond mirrored every one of them in even gentler gradients. The magnificence of the scene moved Nell’s heart, and she appreciatively unlocked the gates of her soul to welcome it.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0047 }

“Dear old world,” she whispered softly, “you possess such great beauty, and it brings me joy to exist within you.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0048 }

Midway down the slope, a tall youth emerged whistling from a gate in front of the Carrow homestead. Hugh was the person, and his whistle faded from his lips when Nell was recognized by him. Courtesy prompted him to lift his cap, yet he intended to keep walking without speaking, had Nell not paused and extended her hand.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0049 }

“Hugh,” she said, her cheeks turning scarlet, “for giving up the school for my sake, I want to express my gratitude. You were very kind to do so—and my wish is for you to know that I am grateful.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0050 }

Hugh enthusiastically grasped the hand that was extended to him.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0051 }

“Nell, my actions were not especially noble. Being of slight assistance to you brought me pleasure. Will friendship exist between us from now on? Is my former misdeed truly pardoned by you?”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0052 }

Nell giggled while attempting in vain to pull back her hand.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0053 }

“Although I was unaware of it then, I pardoned you on that day near the pond landing. What an unyielding little goose I proved to be. Ever since—I might just as well offer a full admission—I have felt regret.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0054 }

“We will end up being the closest of friends,” Hugh stated, filled with joy. “It was our fate to be great friends, Nell. You have resisted fate long enough. I am certain we can assist one another in numerous ways. You plan to continue your studies, don't you? I intend to as well. Come along, I will accompany you on your walk home.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0055 }

When Nell came into the kitchen, Thirza observed her with a look of curiosity.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0056 }

“Nell, who was it that walked up the lane alongside you?”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0057 }

“Hugh Carrow,” replied Nell, annoyed that she was blushing. “I ran into him on Pembroke’s hill.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0058 }

“It surprised me that your friendship with Hugh Carrow was close enough for you to spend thirty minutes chatting with him by the gate,” Thirza remarked, smiling dryly.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0059 }

“We have not been—we have been fine foes. However, we have concluded that being fine friends from now on will prove far wiser. Was our time there truly thirty minutes? It felt like merely a couple of moments. Nevertheless, you understand, we must make up for five years of missed discussions, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0060 }

Nell remained at her window for a considerable time during that night, accompanied by a joyful satisfaction. Softly purring, the wind rustled through the branches of the cherry trees, while scent from the mint rose up toward her. Above the sharp-topped firs down in the hollow, the stars flickered, and Isolde’s light shone across the familiar opening.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0061 }

Her vistas had narrowed from the evening she had been seated in that spot following her return from Regent’s; yet she understood that blossoms of peaceful contentment would flourish by her side, even though her assigned route was destined to be restricted. She was to possess the delight of earnest labor, noble ambition, and harmonious companionship; no one was able to deprive her of her heritage of imagination or her visionary realm of reveries. Furthermore, the turn in the path was ever present!
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0062 }

“‘With God residing in his heaven, everything on earth is as it should be,’” Nell breathed in a quiet tone.
{: #nw-v01-c38-p0063 }
